import pandas as pd

# List all source file paths
source_files = [
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_1/training_0.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_1/training_1.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_1/training_2.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_1/training_3.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_1/training_4.csv"
]

# Read all source tables into a list of DataFrames
dfs = []
for file in source_files:
    df = pd.read_csv(file, index_col=0)
    dfs.append(df)

# All source tables have the same schema as the target:
# ['Registered_Students', 'Time', 'Date', 'Room', 'Room_Capacity', 'Module']
# Actually, source schema is ['Time', 'Date', 'Room', 'Room_Capacity', 'Module', 'Registered_Students']
# Target columns order is: [Registered_Students, Time, Date, Room, Room_Capacity, Module]
# So we need to reorder columns to match target schema.

# Concatenate all source DataFrames (union)
combined_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

# Reorder columns to match target schema
target_columns = ['Registered_Students', 'Time', 'Date', 'Room', 'Room_Capacity', 'Module']
combined_df = combined_df[target_columns]

# The source data contains many NaNs as per examples, but no instructions to filter them out.
# We keep all rows as is.

# Write the combined DataFrame to the target CSV file
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_1/target_multisource_cot.csv"
combined_df.to_csv(output_path, index=False)
